newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-SHEARER WELCOMES BLACKBURN TO COURT OF ST JAMES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SHEARER WELCOMES BLACKBURN TO COURT OF ST JAMES.

text.p: The king of English soccer opens the gates of his new St James's Park palace to his former courtiers on Saturday as title-aspirants Newcastle host 1995 champions Blackburn.
Alan Shearer faces his old club for the first time since his world record-breaking 15-million-pound ($23.3-million) move to Newcastle, well aware he still has critics to silence.

The England striker has scored just one free kick and a penalty in his five league games to date, and drew a blank on Tuesday as Kevin Keegan's side put four goals past Swedish part-timers Halmstad in the UEFA Cup.

Meanwhile, his England partner Les Ferdidand has proved he still has a future at Newcastle, scoring the winnner in the recent northeast derby against Sunderland, and both goals in the 2-1 win at Tottenham last Saturday.

Shearer, adamant he will not sink under the weight of expectation on Tyneside, says he does not care who scores, as long as Newcastle win, and after a shaky start to the season, that is exactly what they are doing.
If England's European championship hero does run riot against his former team mates, Blackburn manager Ray Harford could be left looking for a new job.

English club side managers are dropping like flies this season and Harford, whose side have lost four of their five opening games, scoring just three goals in the process, is widely tipped as the next casualty.

Now their most famous old boy is poised to provide a painful reminder of the finishing prowess which brought Blackburn the league title just two seasons ago. The other premier league manager under pressure is Ron Atkinson, whose Coventry City side are cushioning Blackburn from the foot of the table.

Atkinson, a larger-than-life character who likes to wade into the transfer market in search of big-name signings, spent heavily in the close season, bringing elegant Scotland captain Gary McAllister to Highfield Road.
On Saturday, McAllister faces his old side Leeds, who have just emerged from the current round of managerial musical chairs with former Arsenal boss George Graham at the helm.

Graham, back in football for the first time since London giants Arsenal sacked him in 1995 over illegal payments from transfer deals, may soon be joined at Elland Road by current Arsenal caretaker manager Stewart Houston.

Several English newspapers reported on Friday that Houston, who was only expecting to remain in charge at Highbury until former Monaco boss Arsene Wenger arrives later this year, will quit the Gunners and follow Graham to Leeds.

Arsenal, who face surprise league leaders Sheffield Wednesday in Monday's match, would then be managerless again, little more than a month after they sacked Bruce Rioch, who had only held the post for a year.
Coventry and Leeds both go into Saturday's game reeling from 4-0 defeats last weekend, to Middlesbrough and Manchester United respectively.
Arsenal are in no better frame of mind, despite their bright league start which has seen them lose just once in five games.

They face first-round elimination from the UEFA Cup after their 3-2 home defeat by Borussia Moenchengladbach on Tuesday, and with internal strife again threatening to resurface, Wednesday will be hoping for a fifth victory from six games to keep them top of the division.
